attested.notes: FIRST FULL-PAGE COLD READ. The two earlier reads this session used stranger_read.py, which only ever extracts the opening 500 words; they covered 500 of 7,692 and neither read the second half. This one gave a fresh reader the whole rendered page and asked specifically about the middle and the end. It found more than both earlier reads combined, and most of what it caught was written by me earlier today. Fixed: the answer the reader arrived with (closing does not touch a guarantee you signed or a director loan balance) sat at the very bottom after four thousand words aimed at wealthier readers, and is now stated in the opening with a link to the guarantees guide; the reader said put it near the top and I would have trusted the rest. The instruction to hunt for your signature on a guarantee did not say what a guarantee looks like, so it now describes the document and the tell (signed in your own name rather than for the company) and links to the enforcement guides. The reader came worried about their house and the words house and home appeared nowhere: the section now states that a guarantee makes the debt yours personally and that some guarantees additionally carry a charge over property, without asserting anything about enforcement that the page cannot support. The employees section never answered the reader's actual question, whether staff get paid and whether the shortfall becomes the director's debt; it now does. Six load-bearing terms were used unexplained and the gate's jargon check passed all of them: the Gazette (which I had built a key insight on top of), the Official Receiver, statutory demand, dilapidations, bond premium, and the payroll return acronyms. IP was used for insolvency practitioner in a table before any definition AND for intellectual property twice in the same page; the abbreviation is now defined on first full mention and the intellectual-property uses are spelled out. The 13 pound claim contradicted the cost table, which adds accountant fees and VAT, so it now says the 13 pounds is the filing and not the closure. A signpost now tells an insolvent reader that the two solvent sections do not apply, because that is where the reader put the phone down. Performance lines cut, nearly all of them mine from earlier today: the reason is mechanical rather than moral, nobody chooses it, the invisible ones, you paid the accountant to file the return that generated it, nothing chases you for either, the useful call is todays, and conduct claims are the ones directors worry about, which asserted a fear the reader said was simply wrong. Repetition thinned where the reader counted it. IMPORTANT REVERSAL: the reader counted eight or nine sections opening with a variant of directors call us and said it stops reading as experience and starts reading as advertising. Several of those were added by me in the previous round to lift we-density toward the voice engine's 10-15 target. Two removed. The reader's verdict beats the number, and the density target should not be chased on this page. TWO THINGS A VOICE PASS CANNOT FIX, both escalated to the owner rather than papered over: first, the page still gives no cost figure for a CVL, which is the route this reader was obviously heading for, so every number on the page is for the solvent case; second, the page's shape puts two sections of tax relief detail for shareholders with up to a million pounds of gains between a distressed reader and what they need, and a signpost is a patch on a structural problem.
